title: Allow manual certificate renewal outside the standard renewal period
spec_file: Allow manual certificate renewal outside the standard renewal period.md

explanation.summary: Aujourd'hui, Horizon refuse de renouveler un certificat géré tant que sa période de renouvellement n'est pas ouverte (erreur WEBRA-RENEW-005 « Certificate not in its renewal period »), et aucun opérateur ne peut forcer ce renouvellement. La fonctionnalité ajoute un renouvellement anticipé : un opérateur autorisé peut renouveler un certificat avant l'ouverture de sa fenêtre, seul ou en lot, depuis l'interface (inventaire RA, My Certificates) ou l'API REST. Seule la vérification de la période est levée : la validité et le statut du certificat restent contrôlés. Le certificat renouvelé reste sur le même profil et le même connecteur PKI, conserve ses métadonnées techniques tierces, et l'opération est tracée dans l'événement d'audit LIFECYCLE-RENEW.
explanation.ecosystem_role: Le renouvellement est une action du cycle de vie (CLM) exécutée par Horizon-Core sur un certificat géré, en s'appuyant sur le profil, le connecteur PKI (DigiCert, Sectigo...) et les connecteurs tiers de déploiement (par exemple F5). Le renouvellement anticipé répond à deux situations opérationnelles : une révocation de masse décidée par une autorité de certification, où il faut réémettre des centaines de certificats immédiatement, et une migration de connecteur PKI, où l'on repointe le profil vers la nouvelle autorité puis on renouvelle d'un coup. Les acteurs concernés sont l'opérateur RA (acteur principal), l'administrateur métier (qui décide qui détient la capacité) et le service principal (scripts via l'API). Le renouvellement automatique, planifié ou en libre-service reste régi par la période de renouvellement. Les droits de renouvellement existent déjà par profil (renew, renew_api, request_renew, approve_renew) ; le choix du mécanisme d'autorisation du renouvellement anticipé est une question ouverte de la spec.
example: Une autorité de certification annonce la révocation prochaine d'un lot de certificats. Camille, opérateur RA, doit réémettre immédiatement 12 certificats du profil Web-Prod, dont aucun n'est encore dans sa fenêtre de renouvellement.
Camille ouvre l'inventaire des certificats dans Horizon RA, filtre sur le profil Web-Prod et l'émetteur concerné, puis coche les 12 certificats, comme elle le ferait pour une révocation en masse.
Elle choisit Renew et confirme explicitement qu'il s'agit d'un renouvellement anticipé.

Horizon traite chaque certificat indépendamment. Dix sont renouvelés sur le même profil et le même connecteur, avec le même DN, les mêmes SAN et les mêmes étiquettes. Un certificat est déjà révoqué : il est refusé avec la raison « révoqué », sans bloquer les autres. Un autre est déjà expiré et refusé de la même manière.
Les certificats renouvelés conservent leurs métadonnées techniques tierces : celui qui était déployé dans la partition F5 Common/prod sera redéployé au même endroit.
Plus tard, Louis, administrateur métier, consulte le journal d'audit : chaque événement LIFECYCLE-RENEW de Camille indique que le renouvellement a eu lieu hors période de renouvellement.
Un utilisateur final sans la capacité qui tente la même action sur son propre certificat est rejeté, et son certificat n'est pas renouvelé.
limits: Le renouvellement automatique ou planifié n'est pas modifié ; il reste gouverné par la période de renouvellement.
Le profil et le connecteur PKI ne changent pas lors du renouvellement : pour migrer de connecteur, on repointe d'abord le profil puis on renouvelle.
Pas de période de renouvellement distincte par connecteur.
Un certificat révoqué, expiré ou non renouvelable le reste : seule la période est contournée.
Pas de renouvellement anticipé en libre-service pour l'utilisateur final.
Le mécanisme d'autorisation (réutiliser approve_renew avec approbation obligatoire, ou nouveau droit dédié) n'est pas tranché.

requirements.text: As an RA Operator, I want to renew a managed certificate before its renewal period opens, so that I can respond to a mass-revocation event without waiting for each certificate's window.
As an RA Operator, I want to select several certificates in the certificate inventory and renew them in one action, so that I can reissue hundreds of certificates quickly.
As a Service principal, I want to trigger early renewal through the REST API, so that I can script a CA migration.

As a Business administrator, I want early renewal restricted to authorized operators and recorded in the audit log, so that ordinary users cannot bypass the renewal window and mass events stay reviewable.
As an RA Operator, I want the renewed certificate to keep its third-party technical metadata, so that it redeploys to the same location (for example the same F5 partition).
An authorized operator can renew a managed certificate whose current time is before its renewal period.
Early renewal reissues the certificate on its current profile and PKI connector, following standard renew semantics (same DN, SAN, extensions, labels, metadata; only the key may change).
The renewed certificate retains the previous certificate's third-party technical metadata, so redeployment targets the same location.
An operator can select several certificates in the certificate inventory (RA) and in My Certificates and renew them in one action.
Early renewal is available through the REST API, for a single certificate and for multiple certificates.
In a bulk early renewal, each certificate is processed independently: a failure on one does not stop the others, and per-certificate outcomes are reported.
Early renewal overrides only the renewal-period check; validity and status checks (revoked, expired, renewal not enabled on the profile) still apply and reject ineligible certificates.
Early renewal is restricted to authorized operators and is not part of end-user self-service renewal.
An early renewal is identifiable in the audit log (LIFECYCLE-RENEW) as having occurred outside the renewal period.

Managed certificate outside its renewal period and an authorized operator: a new certificate is issued on the same profile and PKI connector, the previous certificate follows standard renew handling, and the new certificate carries the previous certificate's third-party technical metadata.
Bulk selection containing a revoked certificate: eligible certificates are renewed, the revoked one is rejected with a per-certificate reason, and successful renewals are not rolled back.
A user without the early-renewal capability attempting to renew outside the window is rejected and the certificate is not renewed.
An expired or revoked certificate is rejected on validity or status grounds, not on the renewal-period check, when an authorized operator attempts early renewal.
After an early renewal, the LIFECYCLE-RENEW audit event indicates the renewal occurred outside the renewal period.
Renew a single certificate early: RA Operator, Business administrator, Service principal (API); not available to end-user self-service. Enforcement mechanism open.
Bulk early renewal from RA / My Certificates: RA Operator, Business administrator; per-certificate authorization applies.
Approve an early renewal: RA Operator (approver), only if the approval-based model is chosen.
Backward compatibility: in-window renewal, automatic renewal and self-service renewal are unchanged; early renewal is additive.
Performance: bulk early renewal handles selections of the order of hundreds of certificates without blocking the operator; asynchronous processing is acceptable.
Security: early renewal is a privileged action, every early renewal is audited and identifiable as out-of-window, and tenant isolation applies.
Configuration: no new HOCON configuration; early renewal is a per-request action, not a global toggle.

tests.title: Early renewal of a single certificate by an authorized operator
tests.preconditions: A managed certificate on profile Web-Prod whose renewal period has not started (today is before notAfter minus the profile renewal period). Renewal is enabled on the profile. An RA Operator account holds the early-renewal capability [A: name of the right or permission]. The certificate has labels, an owner and several SAN entries.
steps: As the RA Operator, search the certificate in the certificate inventory and open its details
The details page shows the certificate as valid, with its expiry date and the profile; the renewal period has not started
Click Renew [A: label of the early-renewal action]
A confirmation dialog states that the renewal is outside the renewal period and asks to confirm [A: exact wording]
Confirm the early renewal
The request is created without the error WEBRA-RENEW-005 (Certificate not in its renewal period)
If the profile requires approval, approve the request as the approver [A: depends on the enforcement model, see TC-08]
The request reaches the completed state
Open the new certificate
It is issued on profile Web-Prod and the same PKI connector; DN, SAN, extensions, labels, owner and metadata are identical to the previous certificate; only the key may differ
Open the previous certificate
It follows the standard renew handling of the profile (for example revocation or retention as configured)

tests.title: Third-party technical metadata is kept on the renewed certificate
tests.preconditions: A third-party connector is configured and the certificate was deployed through it, with technical data such as an F5 partition Common/prod [A: use a test connector or a stub]. The certificate is outside its renewal period. The operator holds the early-renewal capability.
steps: Open the certificate details and note the third-party data (connector name, partition or target)
The third-party data of the connector is displayed [A: where it appears in the UI and in the API response]
Renew the certificate early
The request succeeds
Open the renewed certificate and compare its third-party data
The connector and the technical data are identical (same partition Common/prod)
Run the redeployment of the renewed certificate through the connector
It is deployed to the same location as the previous certificate

tests.title: Early renewal through the REST API, single and multiple
tests.preconditions: A Service principal with an API token holding the early-renewal capability. Three managed certificates outside their renewal period on the same profile.
steps: Call the renew endpoint for one certificate without the early-renewal indicator
The request is rejected with WEBRA-RENEW-005, as before the change
Call the renew endpoint for the same certificate with the early-renewal indicator [A: name and location of the indicator]
The request is accepted and a renewal request is created for that certificate
Call the renew endpoint for the two other certificates in one call with the indicator [A: format of the multiple call]
One result per certificate is returned [A: structure of the response]; both renewals are created
Check the resulting certificates in the inventory
Three new certificates exist on the same profile and connector

tests.title: Bulk early renewal with a partial failure, from inventory and My Certificates
tests.preconditions: Ten managed certificates on profile Web-Prod: eight valid outside their renewal period, one revoked, one expired. An RA Operator who owns them or can manage them, with the early-renewal capability.
steps: In the certificate inventory (RA), select the ten certificates with the checkboxes, as for a bulk revocation
The selection counter shows 10 and a Renew action is available [A: position of the bulk Renew action]
Click Renew and confirm the early renewal
The confirmation states the renewal is outside the renewal period; processing starts
Read the outcome of the operation
Eight certificates are renewed; the revoked and the expired certificates are rejected with a per-certificate reason based on status or validity [A: report format and wording]
Check that the eight new certificates still exist after the rejections
None of the successful renewals has been rolled back
Repeat the operation on four other eligible certificates from My Certificates
The same bulk renewal is available and works in My Certificates

tests.title: Validity and status checks still apply to early renewal
tests.preconditions: An authorized operator. A revoked certificate, an expired certificate and a certificate on a profile where renewal is not enabled, all outside any renewal period.
steps: Try an early renewal of the revoked certificate
Rejected because of its status; the error is not WEBRA-RENEW-005
Try an early renewal of the expired certificate
Rejected because of its validity; the error is not WEBRA-RENEW-005
Try an early renewal of the certificate on the profile without renewal enabled
Rejected because renewal is not enabled on the profile
Check the three certificates
None of them was renewed and no new request exists

tests.title: Users without the capability cannot renew outside the window
tests.preconditions: A managed certificate outside its renewal period, owned by an end user. The end user can renew in window. A privileged user without the early-renewal capability.
steps: As the end user, open My Certificates and look at the renew action of the certificate
No early-renewal action is offered in self-service [A: Renew hidden, disabled or showing the period error]
As the end user, call the renew API for this certificate
Rejected; the certificate is not renewed [A: error code, WEBRA-RENEW-005 or an authorization error]
As the privileged user without the capability, try the early renewal from the UI and the API
Rejected; the certificate is not renewed
Grant the capability to the privileged user and retry
The early renewal is accepted

tests.title: Standard renewals are unchanged
tests.preconditions: A certificate inside its renewal period owned by an end user. A certificate outside its period. A certificate linked to an automation policy (metadata AUTOMATION_POLICY). Access to the Horizon configuration.
steps: As the end user, renew the certificate inside its renewal period
The renewal succeeds without any early-renewal confirmation
Let the automatic renewal run on the certificate outside its period
The certificate is not renewed automatically before its period
Renew the automation-policy certificate outside its period with the existing automation bypass
Behaviour identical to the previous version
Look for a new global setting in the configuration and in the HOCON files
No new toggle or HOCON key exists; early renewal is only a per-request action

tests.title: Approval workflow for early renewal
tests.preconditions: [A: the enforcement model is not decided, see Technical Open Question 1] Profile whose renew workflow requires approval. An operator who requests early renewals and an RA Operator approver. Three certificates outside their renewal period.
steps: As the operator, request an early renewal of one certificate
A request waits for approval and the certificate is not renewed yet [A: depends on the model chosen]
As the approver, approve the request
The certificate is renewed
Request another early renewal and deny it as the approver
The certificate is not renewed
As the operator, request a bulk early renewal of the three certificates
[A: one request per certificate, or one global request] Each certificate follows the approval workflow independently

tests.title: Audit event identifies renewals outside the renewal period
tests.preconditions: Access to the audit events as a Business administrator. One early renewal and one in-window renewal performed.
steps: Open the audit events and filter on LIFECYCLE-RENEW
Both events are listed
Open the event of the early renewal
It indicates the renewal occurred outside the renewal period [A: field name or flag] and identifies the operator
Open the event of the in-window renewal
It does not carry the out-of-period indication
Check bulk renewals
Each certificate of a bulk early renewal has its own LIFECYCLE-RENEW event with the indication

tests.title: Tenant isolation of early renewal
tests.preconditions: Two tenants A and B, a managed certificate outside its period in tenant B, an operator with the capability in tenant A, and a root tenant administrator.
steps: As the tenant A operator, try to renew the tenant B certificate through the API with the early-renewal indicator
Rejected as not found or forbidden; no request is created
As the tenant A operator, search the tenant B certificate in the UI
It is not visible
As the root tenant administrator, open the certificate of tenant A
The early-renewal action is visible, as for other lifecycle actions

tests.title: Bulk early renewal of several hundred certificates
tests.preconditions: [A: seed of 300 managed certificates outside their period, created by a seed script] An operator with the capability.
steps: Select the 300 certificates in the inventory and start a bulk early renewal
The screen stays usable; the operation runs asynchronously [A: progress indicator]
Follow the progress and wait for the end
All certificates reach a final outcome; the report lists each outcome [A: expected duration threshold, not defined in the spec]
Search the new certificates
All eligible certificates were renewed, none is duplicated

tests.title: Connector migration: repoint the profile then renew early
tests.preconditions: Profile Web-Prod pointing to PKI connector A, with two certificates outside their period. A second PKI connector B available.
steps: Repoint profile Web-Prod to connector B
The profile is saved with connector B
Renew one certificate early
The new certificate is issued by connector B, on profile Web-Prod; the metadata PKI_CONNECTOR shows connector B
Look in the renewal UI and API for an option to choose another profile or connector
None is offered; the renewal always uses the current profile and connector

open_questions: Mécanisme d'autorisation (Technical Open Question 1 de la spec) : réutiliser approve_renew avec approbation obligatoire, ou créer un droit dédié (par exemple renew_force) ? Conditionne ACT-1, ACT-3, TC-06 et TC-08.
Le renouvellement anticipé exige-t-il toujours l'approbation d'un opérateur RA, en particulier en lot ? (même question ouverte)
Forme de l'indicateur de renouvellement anticipé dans l'API (paramètre, en-tête, champ du corps) et format de la réponse pour plusieurs certificats.
Format du rapport par certificat d'un renouvellement en lot et libellés d'interface (bouton, confirmation).
Seuil de performance du renouvellement en lot et existence d'un indicateur de progression (NFR-2, TC-11).
Traitement du certificat précédent (« standard renew handling ») : dépend du profil ; à confirmer pour le renouvellement anticipé.
Les certificats en lot sans droit individuel : rejet par certificat ou rejet global ? (ACT-2 mentionne une autorisation par certificat).
findings: Un contournement de la période existe déjà dans le code : un certificat portant la métadonnée AUTOMATION_POLICY saute la vérification (WebRARenewRequest.scala:755-759). C'est le seul contournement actuel, conforme à la spec. Le renouvellement anticipé ne doit pas élargir ce contournement (TC-07).

L'erreur WEBRA-RENEW-005 contient en détail la date de début de période (« period starts: ... ») ; elle est aussi listée dans RequestController.scala:56. Elle doit rester identique pour les non autorisés.

Aucun renouvellement en lot n'existe côté interface : la révocation en lot existe (BulkMultipleRevocationPopup.vue, MultipleRevocation.vue, sélection dans MyCertificates.vue et SearchCertificates.vue) et sert de modèle, comme le dit la spec.

Les droits de renouvellement existent par profil (renew, renew_api, request_renew, approve_renew : CertificateProfile.scala:188-253, LifecyclePermission.scala:36-39). Aucun droit de type renouvellement forcé n'existe.

Les métadonnées de renouvellement générées ne contiennent que PKI_CONNECTOR et PREVIOUS_CERTIFICATE_ID (WebRARenewRequest.scala:990-994). La conservation des données tierces (Certificate.thirdPartyData) n'est pas visible dans ce fichier : à vérifier avec le Backend avant de valider TC-02.
Un profil sans période de renouvellement suit une branche distincte (WebRARenewRequest.scala:293) : le comportement exact du refus « renouvellement non activé » est à confirmer pour TC-05.
